content.title: St. John’s University School Of Law - Lexinter
content.text: St. John’s University School of Law stands out among New York law schools for its blend of academic rigor, practical training, and career-focused outcomes. Located in Queens with direct access to Manhattan’s legal market, it offers students a strong platform for internships, clinics, and post-graduate opportunities in one of the nation’s most competitive legal environments. Founded in 1925, St. John’s Law has built a reputation for advocacy, public service, and professional preparation. From its respected clinical programs to its strong bar passage and employment outcomes, the school continues to attract applicants seeking a well-rounded legal education with real-world impact. Must Know Facts Of St. John’s University School Of Law Get to know the key facts that define St. John’s University School of Law, including its academics, student experience, tuition, reputation, and career outcomes. This helps you clearly understand what the school offers and how it aligns with your goals. Location And Campus Situated in Queens, New York City, St. John’s University School of Law benefits from its proximity to one of the world’s foremost legal, business, and cultural hubs. The campus combines traditional and modern architecture and features advanced facilities, including a moot court room, contemporary classrooms, and a spacious law library. The law school’s location near Manhattan’s legal and business institutions provides students with exceptional opportunities for practical learning experiences. They can readily access internships and externships in diverse legal settings, ranging from top-tier law firms and corporations to public interest organizations and governmental agencies. Academic Programs And Curriculum St. John’s University School of Law offers a Juris Doctor (JD) program that combines a strong academic foundation with practical legal training. The program requires 89 credit hours and is available in both full-time and part-time flex day formats, allowing students to balance their studies with other commitments. Alongside rigorous coursework, students gain hands-on experience through externships, co-curricular activities, and opportunities to pursue joint degrees in fields such as business and political science. The law school places a strong emphasis on experiential learning through its comprehensive clinical program. With ten in-house and partner clinics, students work directly with real clients and cases under the supervision of experienced legal professionals. These clinics cover a wide range of areas, including child advocacy, criminal defense, prosecution, and refugee representation, giving students exposure to diverse legal challenges. Programs such as the Defense and Advocacy Clinic and the Consumer Justice for the Elderly: Litigation Clinic allow students to support vulnerable populations while developing practical skills. Additional clinics, including Economic Justice and Refugee and Immigrant Rights Litigation, further highlight the school’s commitment to social justice. Together, these experiences equip students with the courtroom skills, professional insight, and sense of purpose needed for a successful legal career. Admissions And Acceptance Rate St. John’s University School of Law maintains a selective admissions process, seeking applicants with strong academic performance, personal achievements, and a commitment to justice. Candidates must submit LSAT or GRE scores, undergraduate transcripts, personal statements, and letters of recommendation as part of a holistic review. The acceptance rate is 30.6%, reflecting the school’s competitive nature. The median LSAT score is 162, and the median GPA is 3.74, highlighting the strong academic profile and high standards expected of admitted students. Tuition Fee And Financial Aid St. John’s University School of Law sets its tuition and fees at $74,136, reflecting the cost of a private legal education in New York City. Despite the high tuition, the school offers significant financial support to help reduce students’ overall expenses. Around 80.03% of full-time students receive grants or scholarships, with an average award of $70,170. This substantial financial aid helps cover a large portion of tuition, making the program more accessible and easing the financial burden for many students. Rankings And Reputation St. John’s University School of Law is ranked 63rd nationally by U.S. News & World Report and holds the No. 25 position in part-time law programs. The school also performs strongly in key specialties, including Legal Writing (No. 17) and Trial Advocacy (No. 21), reflecting its focus on practical legal skills. Additional rankings include Criminal Law (No. 57), Intellectual Property Law (No. 63), and Business/Corporate Law (No. 78). These recognitions, along with the school’s strong clinical programs and emphasis on professional training, reinforce the school’s reputation for producing skilled, practice-ready legal professionals. Career Prospects And Alumni St. John’s University School of Law boasts an impressive job placement rate, with the majority of graduates securing employment within ten months of graduation. St. John’s University School of Law demonstrates strong outcomes in Bar passage and job placement. The first-time Bar passage rate is 87.1%, exceeding the national average of 82.6%. The school’s ultimate Bar passage rate over two years reaches an impressive 96.7%. St. John’s University School of Law reports that 95.2% of its graduates achieve full-credit employment outcomes within 10 months of graduation. These results highlight the school’s commitment to preparing students for professional success in the legal field. Graduates pursue various career paths, including positions in law firms, corporate legal departments, government agencies, and public interest organizations. The law school’s vast and influential alumni network comprises graduates who have achieved success across diverse fields. Esteemed judges, politicians, and business leaders count among the notable alumni. Through this network, students have abundant opportunities for internships, clerkships, and networking within the legal community, fostering valuable professional relationships and facilitating successful careers. Why Choose St. John’s Law? St. John’s University School of Law offers a strong blend of academic excellence, practical training, and career outcomes, enhanced by its New York City location and supportive alumni network. NYC Advantage Located in Queens, St. John’s Law provides direct access to New York City’s dynamic legal market. Students benefit from proximity to major law firms, courts, corporations, and public agencies. This location creates unmatched opportunities for internships, externships, networking, and real-world legal exposure, helping students build connections and gain experience while still in law school. Strong Alumni Network St. John’s Law has a large and influential alumni network spanning law firms, government, business, and public-interest sectors. These connections open doors to mentorship, internships, and job opportunities. Alumni actively support current students through networking events and career guidance, helping them transition smoothly from law school into successful and meaningful legal careers. Clinical Focus The law school emphasizes hands-on learning through its extensive clinical programs, allowing students to work on real cases under expert supervision. Clinics cover areas like criminal defense, immigration, and economic justice. This practical approach helps students develop essential legal skills, gain courtroom experience, and build confidence, preparing them effectively for real-world legal practice. Career Outcomes St. John’s Law demonstrates strong career outcomes, with a high percentage of graduates securing employment shortly after graduation. Students pursue roles in law firms, government agencies, and public interest organizations. Strong bar passage rates and career support services further enhance employability, ensuring graduates are well-prepared to enter the legal profession and succeed in competitive environments. FAQs About The St. John’s University School Of Law 1. Is St. John’s Law School Considered A Reputable Law School? St. John’s Law School has established a strong reputation as a reputable institution for legal education. It consistently ranks among the top law schools in the United States and has gained recognition for its commitment to public interest law and social justice. 2. What Is The Average LSAT Score For Admission To St. John’s Law School? The average LSAT score for accepted students at St. John’s Law School is around 162. However, the admissions process considers various factors, including undergraduate transcripts, personal statements, and letters of recommendation, in addition to LSAT scores. 3. Does St. John’s University School Of Law Offer Strong Practical Training Opportunities? Yes. St. John’s Law is well known for combining classroom instruction with hands-on legal training through clinics, externships, advocacy programs, and skills-based coursework. Its New York City location further expands access to courts, law firms, public agencies, and public interest organizations for real-world experience. Conclusion St. John’s University School of Law is more than a legal education institution; it’s a community dedicated to social justice and public interest. With a comprehensive curriculum, practical learning opportunities, and an inclusive environment, the law school equips students to navigate the complexities of the legal field. Graduates of this law school carry a strong sense of purpose, using the law to create positive change in various sectors. St. John’s University School of Law fosters ethical legal education and cultivates a new generation of professionals committed to justice and societal impact
